verdict.rationale: Cursor documents several layers of tool-access control. Enterprise admins can control which MCP servers users may run from the dashboard, and servers can be toggled on and off. Run Modes offer an Allowlist mode covering shell, MCP and Fetch calls, CLI permission tokens gate Shell/Read/Write, and hooks such as beforeMCPExecution/preToolUse can block tool calls. Custom subagents can also be given restricted tool access. Missing for 10: detailed docs on how the admin MCP allowlist works (only a one-line claim), explicit admin controls over first-party integrations such as Slack/Linear/GitHub, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
